newsitem.title: JAPAN: JR West spends 19.3 bln yen to help two units.
newsitem.headline: JR West spends 19.3 bln yen to help two units.

text.p: West Japan Railway Co (JR West) said on Monday that it spent a total of 19.3 billion yen in the year to March 31 to help two of its group companies improve their businesses.
The spending is not expected to affect the company's earnings for 1996/97, a company spokesman said.

The units are a golf course operator in Kyoto Prefecture, in which JR West owns a 67 percent stake, and a hotel operator in Okayama Prefecture, in which JR West has about a 90 percent stake, the JR West spokesman said.
Neither of the units, which started operations in 1995, made a profit in fiscal 1996/97, he said.
JR West bought the golf course's clubhouse for 2.7 billion yen and extended interest-free loans to the unit of 5.2 billion yen, the spokesman said.
He also said JR West had bought interior items in the hotel for 11.4 billion yen, he said.
In addition to the 19.3 billion yen in expenditures, JR West also spent about five billion yen in 1996/97 on memberships in the golf course, the spokesman said.
"We bought the memberships not as part of our support for their business but to increase our assets," the JR West spokesman said.
